title: docs(skills): objectstack-ui actions rule teaches the per-record form for a body that writes each selected row
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbGyo1s5XDjcEx7u8WDqbFTx)_
Fixes #36156
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:照着界面技能写「对所选的每条记录各改一次」的批量按钮时,技能现在教「每条勾选记录各执行一次」的写法,不再教「一次拿到全部所选记录、在脚本里循环逐条修改再汇报成败」。同时写明「整批只执行一次」的脚本或流程只会收到调用者自己看得到的记录,最多五千条。
- 为什么做:属于「对外发布的技能包教的内容要和运行时一致」这条线。批量操作的安全加固(所选记录先按调用者的权限读一遍)已经合入并更新了文档,技能文字是它欠下的另一半。
- 出错会怎样:只改技能里的一段文字、一条评测用例和两条待发布说明,不动运行时。写错的话,照着技能生成应用的作者会把批量按钮写成不合适的形式;撤回本次合并即恢复原文。
- 要你做什么:无。

## What changes

State at head `b88dd761` (round 3, three commits). One bullet of `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` (published catalog), one eval case, and two release notes. The wording is derived from `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` as the selection-scope change left it (sections "Declare the bulk dispatch contract" and "Authorization inside an action") and from the runtime; no separate replacement wording exists for this card.

**The bulk bullet under "Visibility, Disable & Feedback"**, replaced in place (one line before, one line after):

- A body that writes each selected row is taught as the per-record form: the list view's `bulkActions: ['NAME']` runs the action once per ticked row, the action declares `execution: 'perRecord'`, and the body writes the row it is handed (`ctx.record`, `ctx.recordId`), pointing at the `crm_create_campaign` example already in the file. A row whose run throws is listed with its message.
- The aggregate form (`bulkActionDefs` entry with `operation: 'custom', execution: 'aggregate'`) is taught as one run for the selection. A script body or a flow receives the ids under the built-in key `params._selectedIds` (`input._selectedIds`), at most 5000 and only ids the caller can read: one the caller cannot read refuses the whole call with `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` before it starts.
- Gone: the sentence teaching an aggregate handler that writes rows one by one, catches per row and returns `{ succeeded, failed }`, and the four id-counting rules that went with it.
- Kept, in one clause: how an aggregate return value is read. Its top-level `succeeded` or `failed` member is read as a `BulkActionResult`, and in any other form (counts, one list) is reported as unreadable. A throw is one outcome for the selection.

**Eval `views-apps-actions-pages.json`, case 23** (a bulk archive where locked tasks refuse). The prompt is unchanged. The expected answer moves to the per-record form: declare `execution: 'perRecord'`, name the action in the list view's `bulkActions`, update only the row the body is handed, and let a locked row fail on its own. `must_contain` is now `perRecord`, `bulkActions: [`, `ctx.record`; `must_not_contain` is `succeeded:`, `{ succeeded` and `{ failed`. Both token lists changed, so the case has a new hash and a regrade sets earlier records of it apart.

**Changeset** `.changeset/36156-actions-per-record-write.md`, `@objectstack/skills` patch.

Not changed: the `list_toolbar` row of the locations table ("one ticked row is its `recordId`, several are refused (no `_selectedIds`)"). It still matches the console (`resolveServerActionRecordId` in `ui/packages/core/src/actions/serverActionHandler.ts`), and the selection-scope change touched no file under `ui/`.

## DELIBERATE CORRECTION

This PR edits one pending release note, `.changeset/34648-skills-result-dialog-bulk-result.md`, so that it stays true once this PR lands in the same release. One sentence pair in its body changes; its front matter, title line and both declaration lines are untouched. `Check Changeset` is red on this PR for that reason, by design, and the PR carries no `skip-changeset` label.

Before:

> A second entry teaches what an `execution: 'aggregate'` bulk handler resolves with when it wrote some rows and refused others, `{ succeeded: string[], failed: [{ id, message }] }`, that it resolves and does not throw, and how the console counts the ids. One eval case for each.

After:

> A second entry says how an `execution: 'aggregate'` bulk handler's return value is read: one with a top-level `succeeded` or `failed` member is read as a `BulkActionResult`, and any other form of those members is reported as unreadable. One eval case for `resultDialog`.

## Why

The action doors now read a record-less call's selection in the caller's own scope before the action runs, and `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` says a body that writes each selected row is best declared `execution: 'perRecord'`. The skill still taught the aggregate form for that body. An AI build that follows the skill should write the per-record form.

## Round 2 (review of `c0072a0a`)

- **S1, eval case 23 tokens.** `must_contain` now holds `bulkActions: [` in place of `bulkActions`, so the answer has to write the per-record wiring itself; `must_not_contain` gained a token for the shorthand return (`succeeded,` in that round, replaced in round 3). The expected answer no longer spells the `{ succeeded, failed }` literal (it would trip the forbidden tokens) and names the half-done answer as wrong. The probe table is under round 3. Measured on the way: `'bulkActionDefs'.includes('bulkActions')` is `false`, so the old token did not match the prompt's own word; the stricter token is still the better one, because it asks for the wiring and not a mention.
- **S2, the aggregate sentence.** "(one zip)" is gone, and the sentence names whose selection is read: "A script body or a flow receives the ids ... only ids the caller can read". An `api` action's selection is not read, and the sentence no longer sits beside an `api`-shaped example.
- **The pending note** is corrected as declared above, and this PR's own note carries the new tokens and the "script body or a flow" wording.

## Round 3 (contract review of `31062c7b`)

- **S1, eval case 23.** The forbidden token `succeeded,` is ordinary English and failed a right answer that says "the rows that succeeded, and ...". It is replaced by `{ succeeded`; `succeeded:` stays.
- **N3, taken in part.** `{ failed` is forbidden too, so a reversed shorthand return is caught. The JSON-quoted wiring (`"bulkActions": [`) is not covered: the grader matches each token as a literal, case-sensitive substring and requires every `must_contain` token, with no alternation, and no single literal matches both spellings while still excluding a bare mention. `bulkActions: [` stays, the TypeScript spelling the skill teaches.
- **N1, taken.** The rule's last sentence now makes the members its subject: "a return value's top-level `succeeded` or `failed` is read as a `BulkActionResult` (...), and in any other form (counts, one list) reported as unreadable". The file is 14842 bytes, 3711 tokens, at its ceiling; no ceiling row moved.
- This PR's own note carries the new forbidden tokens. The corrected pending note is unchanged since round 2.

Token probe at this head (the grader's own rule, applied to seven sample answers):

| sample answer | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `perRecord` added, the aggregate `bulkActionDefs` entry kept | fail, missing `bulkActions: [` |
| per-record wiring, shorthand return of the two lists | fail, forbidden `{ succeeded` |
| per-record wiring, reversed shorthand return | fail, forbidden `{ failed` |
| per-record wiring, keyed return | fail, forbidden `succeeded:` and `{ succeeded` |
| the per-record answer | pass |
| the per-record answer, with the prose "the rows that succeeded, and each locked row ..." | pass |
| the per-record answer with JSON-quoted wiring | fail, missing `bulkActions: [` (the uncovered spelling above) |

## Acceptance notes

- **`BulkActionResult` in the skill, as read from the code.** The console and the audit trail still read it, on an aggregate dispatch only (`readAggregateResult` in `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/hooks/useBulkExecutor.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-invocation-audit.ts`); a per-record run is never read under it. The spec defines its members as the rows the handler wrote and did not write, so its only author is an aggregate body that writes rows, the form this card moves to per-record. What the skill keeps is the reading rule, because it catches any aggregate body: a return value with a top-level `succeeded` or `failed` in another form is reported as unreadable. The shape itself and the id-counting rules are no longer spelled; the type is named with its import path.
- The card's "an aggregate body receives only ids the caller can read" is stated with its mechanism, as the doc states it: no id is dropped, one unreadable id refuses the whole call. Three kinds of call are not read (a declarative update action, a `type: 'api'` action, the system principal); the sentence is scoped to a script body or a flow, the two that are.
- The card's "drop any example that writes rows from an aggregate selection": the file's code examples already carry none (the campaign example is per-record on `main`). The remaining teaching was the prose sentence and eval case 23, both moved here.
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx` and the `bulkActionDefs` description in `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` still describe an aggregate handler that "moved some rows and refused others" answering with a `BulkActionResult`. That is true of the runtime and outside this card. Noted, not filed.
- The dispatch order asked for a five-section 维护者速读; the fleet agent rules fix it at four lines, which is what this body carries.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:

1. `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md`, the last bullet under "Visibility, Disable & Feedback": the per-record sentence, the aggregate sentence (whose selection is read, key, cap, caller-scope refusal), and the kept `BulkActionResult` clause.
2. `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json`, case 23: the expected answer and both token lists.
3. `.changeset/34648-skills-result-dialog-bulk-result.md`: the corrected sentence, against the quotation above.

Two-minute check: `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` prints `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md is 3711 tokens (ceiling 3711; headroom 0)` and exits 0.
